paragraphs.text: Sync DeepSeek Harness model configuration and third-party API keys across machines, over S3-compatib
le storage or WebDAV
# dsh-model-key-sync

Sync your **DeepSeek Harness model configuration and third-party API keys** across
machines, over S3
-compatible storage or WebDAV.

Sign in to Harness on a new computer, pull once, and your custom providers and their
keys are there
— no retyping one key per provider.

> ### Keys are stored in the remote as plaintext
>
> This is deliberate — it matches CC Switch, and

it means a new machine needs no
> passphrase. The consequence is blunt: **anyone who can read that b

ucket or
> collection can read every API key in it.** Use a dedicated application password,
> keep t

he cloud account itself safe, and turn the key toggle off if you only want
> model declarations to t
ravel. See Security.
## Why this exists

Harness keeps each machine's profile, credentials and model declarations locally.
Moving to a second

machine normally means re-entering every provider: display name,
endpoint, protocol, model catalog,

ally means re-entering every provider: display name,
endpoint, protocol, model catalog, and the key.

Other plugins in the ecosystem sync the profile directory and local plugin sources —
`dsh-cloud-sync

` documents that it
deliberately does **not** copy plaintext credentials. That leaves exactly this g

ap:
the keys. This plugin fills it, and carries the model declarations that reference
them.
## Install
Ask the agent in Harness:
> Install the plugin from github:tesths/dsh-model-key-sync
It runs the bundle installer for you. Or point it at a local checkout:
> Install the plugin at /path/to/dsh-model-key-sync
Then reload the page. The section appears under **Settings → Model Key Sync**.

Requires a Harness build that provides the `settings`, `credentials` and `tools`
services, and an `l
lm-pi-ai` (or compatible) model adapter row.
## Configure
**Settings → Model Key Sync**. Cloud sync is the page; a read-only summary of this machine — display
name, API endpoint and model count — sits below it.
### WebDAV
| Field | Value |

| Backend | WebDAV |
| Collection URL | `https://dav.jianguoyun.com/dav/` (nutstore), or your Nextcl

oud path |
| User name | the account's login name (for nutstore: your email) |
| Password | an **app

lication password**, not the login password |
| Remote directory | `dsh-model-key-sync` |
| Sync gro
up | any name; **identical on every machine** |
### S3-compatible

R2, OSS, B2, MinIO and AWS all work. Fill bucket, region (`auto` for R2), endpoint
(blank for AWS),
access key id and secret.
Fill in the fields and press **Save** (configuration and secret save together), then **Test** → **Up
the fields and press **Save** (configuration and secret save together), then **Test** → **Upload**.
### On the second machine

Install the plugin, open the same page, fill the **same** values including the sync
group, and press

**Pull**. The status card lists the credentials it
stored, for example:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Daily use
- **Manual**: upload after editing models under Settings → Models; pull before using another machine

.
- **Auto**: tick *Auto upload*. A pull never triggers an
upload.
- **Conflict**: nothing is overwr

itten silently. When both sides changed, a pull is
refused and the message names the axis — `model r

outes`, `API keys`, or both. Tick
*Force* to take the remote, or upload to keep this device.
## What travels
| Included | Not included |
| Provider routes: display name, protocol, endpoint, model catalog, key reference, provider defaults

(reasoning, input, cache, thinking budgets) | Sessions, attachments, plugin sources |
| The API key

each route's `apiKeyEnv` resolves to | Credits/quota, usage history |
| Your choice of cloud backen
d and sync group | Other settings (theme, shortcuts, …) |

Restoring merges by route name and **preserves fields it did not export** — retry
policy, timeouts,

transport or compatibility switches stay as they are on this
machine.
## Remote layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Payload objects are written first and the manifest last, so a reader never sees a
manifest describin

g objects the writer has not finished uploading. Every object is
verified by size and SHA-256 on dow

nload. Transfers are serialized with a total
timeout, an idle timeout and a response-size cap.
## Security

- Keys leave the machine only through `ctx.credentials.resolve` and are stored
through `ctx.credenti

als.set` — the same seam the model adapter reads.
- They are uploaded **unencrypted**. Treat the rem

ote as a secret store: a private
bucket, an application password you can revoke, no shared folders.

- Turn off *Sync keys* to sync model declarations only.
- Anyone who obtains the remote can use your

keys. Revoke them at the provider if
that happens.
- The local sync state (`~/.dsh/model-key-sync/c

loud-state.json`) stores hashes, not
keys.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`test/host.mjs` starts a real S3-compatible server and a real WebDAV server on
loopback and drives t

wo simulated devices through upload, pull, idempotency, conflict
refusal and forced overwrite. `test

/client.mjs` loads the real client bundle into
jsdom with a faithful `configForms`/`locale`/`slots`

js` loads the real client bundle into
jsdom with a faithful `configForms`/`locale`/`slots` contract.

See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for why the page talks to the Host
the way it does, and CONTRIBUTING.md bef
ore changing that channel.
